rules.reason: docs/vision.md is the constitution and is human-owned. Every other change here is graded against it, so an agent that can edit it can launder any other change past its own grader. Raise the question with the maintainer and stop.

Bare `--force` on a shared remote can silently discard commits that arrived since you last fetched, and that is the one part of pushing which is not recoverable inside a working copy. Use `--force-with-lease`, which is Auto: the lease refuses the push if the remote moved.
Deleting a branch on a shared remote destroys a ref rather than adding one, which is why it is the single push spelling that did not move to Auto on 2026-07-27.

An agent never decides for itself that a change is ready to land. The maintainer may instruct an agent to perform a merge he has decided on; he may not have it decided for him. This is the gate the push gate used to stand in for: a commit enters the repository's record here, not at the push. A merge also has a precondition his approval does not waive: the head must not be behind `main`. Check it with `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/main...<head> --jq .behind_by` — zero, or rebase onto `origin/main`, push with `--force-with-lease`, and let the checks re-run first, because CI tested this branch against a `main` that has since moved.
Repository settings — visibility above all — are Gated. Visibility is also an authorization hold that lives outside this repository entirely.

Branch protection, collaborators and rulesets are changed through the API, not through `gh repo edit` — this repository's own platform floor was configured that way. Gated for the same reason and by the same sentence. `gh api` also reads, and a gated read is a small cost against a settings change nobody approved.
Creating a repository is Gated and outward-facing.

action.none: No single command. `gh repo rename` and a transfer are separate spellings, and a transfer is ordinarily done in the web UI, which no permission rule reaches. Named rather than folded into a neighbouring rule so the gap is visible instead of implied by a sentence that covers more than its matcher does.

rules.reason: Renaming or transferring a repository is Gated and outward-facing.
Deleting a repository is Gated, outward-facing, and the least recoverable action in this list.
Tagging is Gated. A tag is a published claim about what a tree contains, and v0.1.0 was cut deliberately after its fix merged rather than before.
Publishing a release is Gated and outward-facing.
Publishing to a package registry or a plugin marketplace is Gated. It cannot be recalled once it has been fetched.

action.none: No tool-level surface. Buying a domain or spending money happens through a registrar or a payment surface this backend never sees, so no permission rule can reach it. It stays a prompt-level prohibition and a habit.

rules.reason: Anything that spends money is Gated.

action.none: No tool-level surface. 'Send a message or artifact outside this repository on the team's behalf' has no single command to match — it is email, chat, an issue on someone else's tracker. A matcher pretending to cover it would be worse than the honest gap.

rules.reason: Sending anything outward on the team's behalf is Gated.
Opening a pull request is Propose: reversible but consequential. The gate is the maintainer's decision to merge, not his keystroke.
Doctrine, templates, personas and skills change by pull request.
Anything in this workspace, including the gate map and this policy file, changes by pull request.
The Status column and the Session log change by pull request.
Changing a verify recipe is Propose — and relaxing a check is the case to scrutinise hardest, because it is the one change that makes every future green mean less.
Reading anything in the repository, including git history, is unattended.
Creating and editing files on a working branch, in a worktree, is unattended. What makes this safe is the push gate above, not the edit itself.
Committing to a working branch is unattended. Committing to main is refused by the platform floor, which is a rail rather than a rule.

Pushing a working branch, including its first push and a `--force-with-lease` rewrite, is unattended as of 2026-07-27. A working branch is visible but is not yet a claim on the repository; the guarantee the push gate stood in for lives at the merge. `main` is refused by the platform regardless. The two Gated spellings above are narrower prefixes and are matched first.
Running a verify recipe, or any read-only shell command, is unattended.
